Text recovered from the Hartshorne, Tenenbaum & Pinker (2018) Cognition SI (Elsevier mmc1.pdf), 'Materials' pp.45-57 and 'Scoring' pp.58-60. The quiz administered 132 items (8 sentence-picture matching + 124 grammaticality judgments across Questions 9-35); the live table holds only the 95 'critical' dialect-invariant items, because data/criticalperiod_syntax.R reads full.csv, which is HTP's already-scored data_for_analysis.csv - the 37 dialect-varying items were dropped upstream by the study's own processing.R. Original question/option numbering is preserved (q4, q8, q9_2, q10_1, q10_3, ... are simply absent), so no renumbering was needed and nothing was padded to reach 95. Chen & Hartshorne (2021) describe the quiz as '135 grammaticality judgments, 95 of which were dialect-invariant'; HTP 2018 says 132 items - the 132/135 discrepancy is between the two papers and does not affect the 95 shipped here. resp is scored accuracy (0/1) against the SI answer key, not the option the respondent chose, so option_text is blank for both levels and correct_response is 1 for every item. The six picture items (q1,q2,q3,q5,q6,q7) get the sentence as item_text; the picture pair itself is not reproducible as text. q33_5 is transcribed exactly as printed, 'Sally swam two miles. Wore a pair of 100 goggles.' - the missing '$' is in the source PDF, confirmed against the page image. The block instruction 'Fill in the blank (Choose all that apply)' was prefixed to each Q11-Q31 stem in section_prompt with ': ' because it is section-scoped rather than table-wide; instructions is left blank for that reason. Note irw::irw_fetch() on this table pulls 107,483,095 rows and times out intermittently - the item/resp gate was also confirmed directly against Redivis.
